newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jerusalem mayor goes on trial for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem mayor goes on trial for fraud.

text.p: Ehud Olmert, the Israeli mayor of Jerusalem and a leading figure in the ruling Likud party, went on trial on Tuesday accused of campaign financing fraud in the 1988 election.

"Although I am not accused of doing anything for myself or acting to benefit personally, the accusations are incorrect and I believe this too will be proven," Olmert, 51, told reporters at Tel Aviv District Court.

Olmert, a political ally of Likud Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, insisted he had no part in an alleged fictitious public relations firm set up to receive and disguise corporate donations barred by law. Olmert was Likud treasurer at the time.

The charge sheet said Olmert "intentionally misled the State Comptroller" by "hiding the fact that Likud received, against the provisions of the Campaign Funding Law, contributions from Israeli corporations".

Trials of public figures on corruption or fraud changes often last for years but Olmert said: "We are interested in as speedy and short a trial as possible. There is no point in stretching anything out."

Olmert was a cabinet minister and government spokesman under former prime minister Yitzhak Shamir. He won an upset victory in 1993 over octogenarian Teddy Kollek, who had been mayor of the holy city for more than 27 years.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it. Palestinians in East Jerusalem have long refused to vote in municipal elections, viewing the city's east as capital of a future independent state.
A court spokesman said the trial would resume on February 9.
